Second, the translation function TRANS maps every PBV-term to an integer term denoting its unsigned value: each bit-vector variable x becomes an integer variable χ(x) with the range constraint 0≤χ(x)<exp(2,κ(x)), where κ(x) is an integer variable for the width of x. Arithmetic operators are translated to their integer counterparts modulo exp(2,k), e.g., TRANS(x+By)=(TRANS(x)+TRANS(y))modexp(2,k) for a common width k. Shifts become multiplications and divisions by exp(2,t), and concatenation, extraction and extension become arithmetic over powers of two of the respective widths. Finally, the bitwise operators are expressed via &N, using the identities x∣y=x+y−x&y and x⊕y=x+y−2⋅x&y to eliminate disjunction and exclusive or. The constraints collected by Adm are translated alongside the formula.
note: As in [SAT'25], except that mod is translated to the internal total modulo operator of cvc5.
